newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 24.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) showed serious shortages in core sector inputs. The latest statistics reveal the core sector further deteriorated during the December 1996-February 1997 period, the Economic Times reports.

Indigenous crude production fell during the period by three percent from the April-December 1996 figures. Power generation fell short by 1.4 percent, coal by 2.1 percent, fertilisers by five percent, saleable steel by five percent and cement by 0.8 percent, the paper says.
** The United States is critical of India's trade policies and tariff structure despite a 'dream budget' for 1997/98 (April-March), the Economic Times reports.

The National Trade Estimate of India (1997) noted that despite recent tariff reductious and relaxation of quantitative curbs, restrictions on consumer goods imports, quantitative restrictions under the restricted imports list and high tariffs remained serious impediments to U.S. trade, especially in agricultural and consumer items.
** Hutchison Max, the cellular telephone licence holder for Bombay, has decided to shelve its proposed $125 million ADR issue, the Observer says.

Several factors, including underpricing of the issue by global investors, were understood to have forced the company to wrap up the issue. Hutchison Max is now weighing other options such as a term loan, private placement and equity participation for alternate funding, the paper says.
MARKETS:
** Indian shares ended with small gains on Wednesday, after late profit-taking erased earlier sharp advances, traders said.
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index .BSESN ended 28.36 points, or 0.75 percent, higher at 3,828.99, off 3,864.77, the day's high.
** The National 50-stock index .NSEI edged up over one percent to close at 1,071.05.
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** Cadbury India's 590 million rupee rights issue will open on May 28 and close on June 24, the Business Standard reports. The paper says the issue will be priced at 140 rupees per share and lead managed by Citibank.

The rights issue is being made in the ratio of one share for every five shares held and 3.96 million shares will be issued. The issue will increase Cadbury's equity to 150 million rupees from 120 million, the paper says.
** The Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) is expected to record a sharp decline in net profit for 1996/97 (April-March), according to a report by the Steel Ministry released on Wednesday.
The ministry said net profit in 1996/97 (April-March) was estimated at 6.53 billion rupees, down from 13.19 billion in the previous fiscal year.
For 1997/98, net profit is projected at 7.40 billion rupees, the ministry said in its annual performance budget.
SAIL shares ended 1.75 rupees below the day's high of 24.25 at the Bombay exchange.
